markets.asOf: ASX close Mon 9 Nov; Wall Street at midday Mon (New York)
markets.note: Wall Street bounced about 2% as investors bought back into AI chip stocks after last week's rout, even as Nvidia fell around 5% on its CEO probe, while Brent slid on reports of a possible Hormuz deal.

lead.headline: Victorian Labor falls to 18% as One Nation moves into second place
lead.body: A DemosAU poll for the Herald Sun puts the Coalition on 33% of the primary vote, One Nation on 21%, Labor on 18%, and the Greens on 17%, with the Coalition ahead 56 to 44 after preferences. Labor's vote has dropped seven points since September, and Labor leader Ben Carroll trails Liberal leader Jess Wilson 48 to 30 as preferred premier. Carroll refused to be drawn on the result, while some Labor MPs voiced concern and others scepticism about the poll.
lead.why: With the election on 28 November, the poll points to a change of government in Victoria and a One Nation vote big enough to shape preferences in outer-suburban seats.
points: Labor's 18% is described as an all-time low for the party in Victoria.
Two-party preferred: Coalition 56, Labor 44, from 52 to 48 previously.
A separate Pakenham seat poll had One Nation on 40% of the primary vote.
The Big Build royal commission into CFMEU influence is holding public hearings during the campaign.

lead.headline: Iran hits tankers in Hormuz as reports of a Qatari-brokered deal push oil lower
lead.body: The Revolutionary Guards say three 'non-compliant' tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, while the US military says it disabled a vessel trying to breach its naval blockade of Iran. Israeli media report that Iran has approved a Qatari-brokered interim deal to reopen the strait in return for the US lifting its blockade and releasing US$8 billion in frozen funds, but neither government has confirmed it. Brent crude fell 3.6% overnight to about US$94 a barrel.
lead.why: Hormuz has been shut for most of the year, so any reopening would ease fuel prices and the inflation that has driven five Australian rate hikes.
points: Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Iran's demands 'outrageous and ridiculous' and said a breakthrough is not close.
Trump said renewed US strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely' if talks produce a strong agreement.
The US has launched Task Force Iron Gate to choke weapons flows through Iran's land borders and the Caspian.
Brent fell 16% last week, its steepest weekly drop since early 2020.

lead.headline: Cabinet hunts budget savings as polls put One Nation level with Labor
lead.body: Cabinet's expenditure review committee met on Monday to find savings for the mid-year budget update, with the $7 billion home battery subsidy, electric vehicle incentives, and departmental spending all in view. The search follows last week's rate hike, with RBA Governor Michele Bullock blaming public and private spending for excess demand. Monday's polls had Labor on 28% in Resolve and 26% in Redbridge, where One Nation led on 28%.
lead.why: Spending cuts aimed at taking pressure off inflation could shape whether rates peak at 4.85%, but they land on a government already sliding in the polls.
points: The battery program was first costed at about $2 billion and has installed more than 600,000 systems.
Murray Watt urged colleagues to stop 'undermining and leaking' against Treasurer Jim Chalmers.
The mid-year update is due in mid-December.
Opposition Leader Angus Taylor announced a 'red tape razor gang' for business regulation.

lead.headline: Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi as hacked data suggests up to 450,000 Russian war deaths
lead.body: US, Ukrainian, and Russian negotiators begin two days of talks in Abu Dhabi today, the fourth round this year, with post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, and humanitarian issues on the agenda. Hacker groups say death records taken from Russia's statistics agency show between about 394,000 and 450,000 deaths linked to the war since February 2022. Rosstat admits cyberattacks but denies any data leaked, and the figures have not been independently verified.
lead.why: The leak, if genuine, would put Russia's losses well above independent counts, adding to pressure on Moscow as it negotiates.
points: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to lead the US delegation.
The independent Mediazona count of identified Russian military deaths stood at 285,881 on 6 November.
Ukraine struck Russia's Kirishi refinery on the eve of the talks.

lead.headline: Trump questions whether the midterms were 'honest' after Democrats take Congress
lead.body: Donald Trump asked on Truth Social whether 'this Election' was honest, blaming early voting 'dumps' and voting machines without evidence, after earlier saying he accepted the results. Democrats flipped both the House and the Senate last week, taking at least seven Republican-held Senate seats and more than 40 House seats. In a 60 Minutes interview he attributed the losses to not being on the ballot, opposition to the Iran war, and some candidates.
lead.why: A president at odds with a hostile Congress for his final two years changes how much the US can commit on Iran, Ukraine, and trade.
points: More than 54 million Americans voted early.
Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska were still uncalled.
House and Senate Republicans choose their new minority leaders on Tuesday.

items.headline: Big Build royal commission hears CFMEU threatened to 'smash' a subcontractor
items.body: Public hearings began with the lead-up to a 2022 stop-work at a Sunbury level crossing removal site, and counsel said the union enjoyed 'a significant level of influence' over the Victorian government.
items.why: The hearings run through the Victorian campaign and go to how billions in public infrastructure money was managed.

items.headline: TikTok grilled over self-harm content at digital duty of care inquiry
items.body: Senator David Pocock questioned TikTok executives over reports of self-harm content as a Senate inquiry examines the government's Digital Duty of Care bill.

items.headline: Families face 'inhumane' choices as aged care beds run short
items.body: In South Australia, which has the longest waits, some families are waiting years for a residential aged care bed, including one man with worsening dementia who has waited two years.

items.headline: ACCC targets fake countdown timers ahead of Black Friday
items.body: The consumer watchdog is cracking down on bogus countdown timers, false 'storewide' discount claims, and misleading price comparisons before the November sales.

items.headline: NSW inmate complaints surge 60% amid lockdowns
items.body: Complaints from NSW prisoners have risen 60% as a growing remand population, lockdowns, and device shortages strain the corrections system.

items.headline: Eisenkot courts Netanyahu's allies as he tries to form Israel's government
items.body: President Isaac Herzog has asked Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a government after last month's election left the Knesset deadlocked, and the former military chief is reaching out to parties from Netanyahu's bloc.
items.why: A government without Netanyahu would be the biggest shift in Israeli politics in years, with direct consequences for Gaza and the Iran war.

items.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for hacking supermarket fridges
items.body: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot says an IRGC-linked cyber unit heated up fridges and freezers in more than 1,000 stores last month, and has vowed European sanctions.

items.headline: ANC records its worst-ever result in South Africa's local elections
items.body: President Cyril Ramaphosa says the verdict must be respected, as the country moves further from the era of ANC dominance towards fragmented coalition politics.

items.headline: Pope Leo rebukes Milei's austerity before a record Buenos Aires crowd
items.body: More than 2.5 million people attended the Pope's Mass in Buenos Aires after he told President Javier Milei the economy must benefit everyone.

items.headline: More than 50,000 displaced by Ethiopia border clashes
items.body: Families are arriving in Kenya with little food or shelter after deadly fighting on the border, and host communities are struggling to cope.

items.headline: Republicans pick their new minority leaders on Tuesday
items.body: After losing both chambers, House and Senate Republicans vote on new leadership teams as the party absorbs the scale of its midterm defeat.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds while Nvidia sheds US$330 billion
items.body: US indexes rose about 2% at midday as chip stocks recovered from last week's AI sell-off, but Nvidia fell as much as 8% after opening an investigation into reports linking chief executive Jensen Huang to a suspected Chinese spy; China calls the claims baseless.
items.why: Nvidia is the largest single holding in most global index funds, so a governance scandal there moves diversified ETFs like VDHG and GHHF.

items.headline: Oil drops below US$95 on Hormuz deal hopes
items.body: Brent fell 3.6% to about US$94 and WTI 3% to US$88 on reports of an interim Iran deal, although Gulf benchmark Murban rose as tanker attacks continued.

items.headline: ANZ falls 3.2% despite a $7.3 billion profit
items.body: ANZ's full-year result dragged the banks lower on Monday, while miners, led by uranium and gold stocks, pushed the ASX 200 up 0.1% to 9,030.

items.headline: ASIC warns over telemarketers pushing super switches
items.body: Unlicensed lead generators are cold-calling Australians to move their super into riskier schemes, prompting a warning from the corporate regulator.

items.headline: RBA flags AI-driven spending as an inflation risk
items.body: The Reserve Bank is watching whether AI investment lifts spending faster than the economy can produce goods and services, adding to inflation pressure.

items.headline: Home values fall for a seventh straight month
items.body: Cotality's index fell 1.2% nationally in October and is 6.7% below its March peak, with Brisbane down 2.0%, Perth 1.7%, and Sydney 1.6% for the month. Vendor discounting is the largest since 2019 and homes are taking a median 39 days to sell.
items.why: Buyers have more stock and more bargaining power than at any time in years, as rate rises cut borrowing capacity.

items.headline: Home battery subsidy in the budget razor's sights
items.body: The $7 billion Cheaper Home Batteries scheme, originally costed at about $2 billion, could be means-tested as the government looks for savings, alongside EV incentives.

items.headline: Older women offered $120,000 homes on 50-year leases
items.body: An Australian-first co-housing project in Queensland aims to give single older women facing housing insecurity an affordable, secure place to live.

items.headline: Bathla workers speak out after the developer's collapse
items.body: Former staff of the collapsed Sydney developer describe unpaid wages and mounting financial hardship.

items.headline: NEJM: on-scene ECPR doubles survival in young refractory cardiac arrest
items.body: In the Dutch ON-SCENE stepped-wedge study (n=231, aged 18 to 50), helicopter teams able to start ECPR on scene achieved 40% survival to discharge versus 20% with conventional care (OR 2.72), and good neurological outcome at six months in 36% versus 13%. Takeaway: a strong signal for taking ECMO to the patient, but it is non-randomised, so causation is not proven.
items.why: It shifts the ECPR debate from 'load and go' to bringing the circuit to the kerb, a model that would need HEMS and retrieval services to redesign how they respond.

items.headline: FDA orders NAION warnings on GLP-1 drugs
items.body: Makers of GLP-1 receptor agonists including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound must add non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy to label warnings, based on trial, animal, and postmarketing data. Novo's European label puts the risk at up to 1 in 10,000, and both companies dispute a causal link; sudden painless monocular vision loss on a GLP-1 warrants urgent review.

items.headline: NEJM: pelacarsen cuts Lp(a) 78% but not cardiovascular events
items.body: Lp(a)HORIZON randomised 8,323 people with Lp(a) of at least 70 mg/dL and found no difference in major adverse cardiovascular events despite a 78% fall in Lp(a). Takeaway: Lp(a) stays a risk marker rather than a proven treatment target for now.

items.headline: NEJM: IL-6 blockade with ziltivekimab fails in ZEUS
items.body: In 6,376 patients with atherosclerosis, CKD, and hsCRP of at least 2 mg/L, ziltivekimab cut hsCRP by 64% but MACE was 17.6% versus 17.7% (HR 0.99), with more serious infections (20.4% vs 17.9%). Takeaway: lowering inflammation markers did not prevent events in this group and came at an infection cost.

items.headline: Grattan finds psychiatrists and paediatricians most likely to charge 'extreme' fees
items.body: A new Grattan Institute report finds some specialists charge up to triple the fees of their peers, with psychiatry and paediatrics among the worst offenders.

items.headline: RACGP pitches a fix for NSW specialist queues before the state election
items.body: With the NSW election in March, the college is calling on parties to commit to cutting waits for specialist appointments.

items.headline: 2026 on track to be the hottest year on record
items.body: Scientists predict this year could beat the record as COP31 opens, with the 1.5C warming limit now close to being overshot.
items.why: A super El Niño year on top of long-term warming means a high-risk summer for heat, fire, and health services.

items.headline: NASA calls for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
items.body: Applications for the next astronaut class close on 3 December, with NASA pitching the role as shaping humanity's future in space.

items.headline: Sanctuary built for the last lowland Leadbeater's possums
items.body: With only a handful of Victoria's lowland Leadbeater's possums left in the wild, conservationists hope a purpose-built sanctuary will help the species recover.

items.headline: Jockey Izzy Neale fighting for life in Dubbo Hospital
items.body: The 22-year-old apprentice is in a critical condition after a serious fall at the Warren races, and tributes are flowing from the racing community.

items.headline: Central West preschools face funding cuts of up to $437,000
items.body: Local preschools say the NSW Universal Preschool Funding model, hailed as a win in Sydney, threatens them with major shortfalls.
items.why: Cuts to community preschools hit regional families who have few alternatives.

items.headline: Four local doctors among eight new Dubbo VRA rescuers
items.body: Eight new members, including four locally trained doctors, have joined the Dubbo VRA Rescue squad.

opinion.title: Labor will have to change tactics if Andrew Hastie leads the Liberals
opinion.author: Patricia Karvelas
opinion.gist: As Labor wears the backlash to bad economic news, a Hastie-led opposition built to fight One Nation's rise would force Labor to rethink its attack lines.

opinion.title: Victorian Labor: a 'credibility-free' zone
opinion.author: Dight Canning
opinion.gist: Federal Labor MPs are right to keep their distance from a Victorian government that has squandered voters' trust.

opinion.title: What's more powerful than the politics of division? Actually listening to people
opinion.author: Julianne Schultz
opinion.gist: The US midterms show populism and big-money politics are not inevitable, and Australian leaders should take note.

opinion.title: Australia's climate minister is about to walk a diplomatic tightrope at COP31
opinion.author: Matt McDonald
opinion.gist: Chris Bowen cannot credibly claim climate leadership while Australia's fossil fuel exports keep driving warming.

opinion.title: Yalta 2.0: A Trump-Xi-Putin summit has little upside for Beijing
opinion.author: Alicja Bachulska
opinion.gist: A three-way summit would let Washington look powerful but could cost China dearly in Europe.

opinion.title: New Zealand's foreign policy could change, but we won't know for weeks
opinion.author: Anna Fifield
opinion.gist: Election limbo across the Tasman will cost New Zealand a voice at APEC and COP just as the region's strategic picture shifts.

stories.headline: Warner backs Khawaja's Sandpapergate claims
stories.body: David Warner says Usman Khawaja's account that wider knowledge of the 2018 ball-tampering plan existed is '100 per cent accurate', and called Cricket Australia's original investigation 'rushed and botched'.

stories.headline: Liverpool win at Selhurst Park to sit fourth
stories.body: Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz, and Alexander Isak scored in a 3-1 win over Crystal Palace that leaves Liverpool fourth on 18 points heading into the international break.

stories.headline: Wallabies thrashed by England for a third straight heavy loss
stories.body: England scored seven tries at Twickenham and inflicted a record points tally on Australia, leaving coach Les Kiss seven days to turn things around before Scotland.

radar.detail: Australia v New Zealand, women's and men's, Brisbane

radar.detail: Coalition leads 56 to 44 in the latest poll

radar.detail: Next class to live and work on the Moon

tidbit: The 2018 Sandpapergate bans were 12 months each for Steve Smith and David Warner and nine months for Cameron Bancroft, and Warner was also barred from ever holding a leadership role in the Australian team.

chapters.title: Welcome
chapters.text: Good morning Chris, and welcome to your briefing for Tuesday the tenth of November. This morning: a brutal new poll for Victorian Labor, with One Nation now ahead of it. Iran sets tankers alight in the Strait of Hormuz, even as reports of a deal send oil lower. Federal cabinet goes hunting for savings as Labor slides in the polls. Ukraine peace talks open in Abu Dhabi today, alongside a hacked estimate of Russia's war dead. And Donald Trump questions whether the midterms were honest. Then a quick lap of the world, the markets, some big heart trials, and news from home.

chapters.title: Victoria's poll shock
chapters.text: We start in Victoria, where Labor has hit a new low less than three weeks from polling day. A DemosAU poll for the Herald Sun has the Coalition on thirty three per cent, One Nation on twenty one, Labor on just eighteen, and the Greens on seventeen. That's a seven point drop for Labor since September. After preferences, the Coalition leads fifty six to forty four, and Liberal leader Jess Wilson leads Labor's Ben Carroll as preferred premier, forty eight to thirty. One seat poll in Pakenham even had One Nation on forty per cent. Carroll wouldn't be drawn on the numbers, and some of his MPs are worried while others doubt the poll. Add the royal commission into the construction union's influence, which is holding public hearings right through the campaign, and it's a hard road to the twenty eighth of November.

chapters.title: Iran and the Strait of Hormuz
chapters.text: To the Gulf. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, calling them non-compliant ships using an unauthorised channel. The US military says it disabled a vessel trying to break its naval blockade of Iran, and Washington has set up a new task force to choke off weapons coming in over land and across the Caspian. Yet oil fell. Israeli media are reporting that Iran has approved a Qatari-brokered interim deal: reopen the strait, in return for the US lifting its blockade and releasing about eight billion US dollars of frozen funds. Neither side has confirmed it, and Marco Rubio called Iran's demands outrageous. Still, Brent slid more than three and a half per cent overnight to around ninety four US dollars a barrel. For us, that matters at the bowser, and for inflation.

chapters.title: Canberra's budget razor
chapters.text: That inflation is why federal cabinet's razor gang met yesterday. After last week's fifth rate hike of the year, the government is looking for savings for its mid-year update in December. On the table: the home battery subsidy, which was first costed at about two billion dollars and is now around seven billion, electric vehicle incentives, and spending across departments. It's happening as Labor's polling slumps. Resolve has Labor on twenty eight per cent, and Redbridge has One Nation ahead on twenty eight, with Labor on twenty six. Environment Minister Murray Watt has told colleagues to stop leaking against Treasurer Jim Chalmers. The question is whether cuts now can help rates peak at four point eight five per cent.

chapters.title: Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
chapters.text: Today, negotiators from the United States, Ukraine, and Russia sit down in Abu Dhabi for two days of talks, the fourth round this year. Security arrangements after the war, de-escalation, and humanitarian issues are on the agenda, and Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to lead for the Americans. In the background, two hacker groups say they took death records from Russia's statistics agency showing somewhere between about three hundred and ninety four thousand and four hundred and fifty thousand deaths linked to the war. Russia admits the cyberattack but denies any leak, and nobody has verified the data. For comparison, the independent count of named Russian soldiers killed sits at about two hundred and eighty six thousand.

chapters.title: Trump and the midterms
chapters.text: In the United States, Donald Trump has asked online whether last week's midterm election was honest, blaming early voting and voting machines, without evidence. On election night he said he accepted the result. Democrats flipped both houses of Congress, taking at least seven Senate seats and more than forty in the House. Speaking on Sixty Minutes, Trump blamed not being on the ballot, opposition to the Iran war, and some weak candidates. Republicans choose their new minority leaders today. Two years of a hostile Congress will shape what America can commit on Iran, Ukraine, and trade.

chapters.title: Around the world
chapters.text: Quickly around the world. In Israel, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government and is reaching out to some of Benjamin Netanyahu's allies. France has blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for hacking the fridges in more than a thousand supermarkets, and wants European sanctions. South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst ever result in local elections. Pope Leo rebuked Argentina's President Milei over austerity, then drew more than two and a half million people to Mass in Buenos Aires. And more than fifty thousand people have fled border fighting in Ethiopia into Kenya, arriving with little food or shelter. Closer to our region, New Zealand's election result is still in limbo, which means it will miss out on a full voice at APEC and the climate talks while it waits.

chapters.title: Markets
chapters.text: Markets. The ASX two hundred finished up a tenth of a per cent at nine thousand and thirty yesterday, with miners and uranium stocks carrying the index while ANZ fell more than three per cent despite a seven point three billion dollar profit. Overnight, Wall Street bounced around two per cent by the middle of the session, as investors bought back into chip stocks after last week's AI sell-off. The exception was Nvidia, down around five per cent after opening an investigation into reports its chief executive was close to a suspected Chinese spy. Because Nvidia is the biggest single stock in most global index funds, that's worth watching in your index funds. The Aussie dollar is just under sixty nine US cents, gold is around four thousand one hundred and twenty three US dollars an ounce, and Bitcoin is down at about seventy four thousand eight hundred. On property, Cotality's index shows home values fell another one point two per cent in October, the seventh monthly fall in a row. Brisbane, Perth, and Sydney are leading the decline, homes are taking a median thirty nine days to sell, and vendors are discounting more than at any time since twenty nineteen. If you're watching the market from Dubbo, buyers have rarely had this much leverage.

chapters.title: Health and medicine
chapters.text: Health and medicine, and the American Heart Association meeting has delivered. The standout for you: a Dutch study of helicopter teams starting heart-lung bypass at the scene in patients aged eighteen to fifty in refractory cardiac arrest. Survival to discharge was forty per cent, against twenty per cent with conventional care, and good neurological recovery at six months was thirty six per cent against thirteen. It isn't randomised, but it's a strong signal. Less happily, two big bets on residual risk failed. Pelacarsen cut lipoprotein little a by seventy eight per cent with no drop in heart attacks or strokes, and the interleukin six blocker ziltivekimab lowered inflammation but not events, with more serious infections. The FDA has also ordered warnings about a rare optic nerve stroke onto weight loss and diabetes drugs including Ozempic and Mounjaro. The risk is small, but sudden painless vision loss in one eye needs urgent review. And at home, the Grattan Institute says psychiatrists and paediatricians are among the specialists most likely to charge extreme fees.

chapters.title: Dubbo and the Central West
chapters.text: Closer to home. Apprentice jockey Izzy Neale, who is twenty two, is fighting for her life in Dubbo Hospital after a serious fall at the Warren races, and tributes are pouring in. Central West preschools say the state's new funding model could cost some of them up to four hundred and thirty seven thousand dollars. And Dubbo's volunteer rescue squad has welcomed eight new members, four of them locally trained doctors.

chapters.title: Sign-off
chapters.text: In sport, Liverpool won three one at Crystal Palace to sit fourth going into the international break, David Warner has backed Usman Khawaja's claims that more people knew about the twenty eighteen ball tampering plan, and the one day series against England starts in Perth on Friday afternoon. That's your morning briefing, Chris. Your evening edition lands at six tonight, with the first day of the Abu Dhabi talks and how Wall Street finished. Have a great day.
